observations: Photo 0 shows a large office photocopier wrapped in clear plastic shrink wrap sitting on a wooden pallet.
The front label in photo 0 reads "SHARP AR-M207".
Photo 1 shows the same machine from the side with "SHARP" visible and a blue "digital" sticker; A4 and A3 paper trays are visible at the bottom.
Photo 2 shows the front again with "SHARP AR-M207" clearly legible.
The seller's text mentions "London use" and states "The model is M307", but the photos show AR-M207.

claims.evidence: No photo or document shows origin or previous location.
Photos 0 and 2 show the model label as AR-M207, not M307.

claims.claim: Packed with an extensive range of superb performance functions
claims.evidence: Marketing text cannot be verified from photos; functions cannot be tested remotely.

risks.risk: Machine may not power on or perform any copy/print function.
risks.proof: Video of the machine powering on, showing ready status, and making a test copy.

risks.risk: Internal consumables (drum, developer, rollers) may be worn or near end of life.
risks.proof: Close-up photos of the interior, scanner glass, and document feeder with plastic wrap removed.

risks.risk: Missing power cable, toner cartridge, paper trays, or manuals.
risks.proof: Photo showing all included accessories laid out next to the machine.

risks.risk: Plastic wrap may conceal external damage, cracks, or broken parts.
risks.proof: Photos of the exterior with the shrink wrap removed.

proof_requests: Video showing the machine powering on and making a test copy.
Close-up photos of the scanner glass, document feeder, and interior with plastic removed.
Photo of all included cables, toner, and trays.
response.reason: The photos clearly identify a Sharp AR-M207 photocopier; despite unverified condition and the seller's model mismatch, it can be priced at its worst case as a used photocopier.
